instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger garlic paste, lemon juice, 1/2 tsp garam masala, chili powder, turmeric powder, and 1/2 tsp salt. Mix well to coat the chicken. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Melt 1 tbsp butter in a large pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken and cook in batches until browned on all sides and mostly cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt the remaining 3 tbsp butter. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tbsp ginger garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Gravy
instructions.text: Stir in the crushed tomatoes, the remaining 1/2 tsp garam masala, and soaked cashews. Add 1/2 cup water. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Stir occasionally.

instructions.title: Blend the Gravy
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the tomato and cashew mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. For an extra silky gravy, you can pass it through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan. This step is crucial for authentic texture.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the smooth gravy to the pan over medium-low heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces, honey or sugar, and heavy cream. Stir gently to combine. Simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to warm through and absorb the flavors. Crush the dried fenugreek leaves between your palms and stir into the curry. Taste and adjust salt if needed.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Garnish with fresh cilantro and a swirl of extra cream, if desired. Serve hot with basmati rice, naan bread, or roti for a complete and satisfying Indian meal.

tips: For the best flavor, marinate the chicken overnight. The longer the marination, the more tender and flavorful your chicken will be.

Do not skip blending the gravy until super smooth. This is key to achieving the signature silky texture of restaurant-style Butter Chicken. Straining it afterwards ensures no cashew or onion bits remain.
Always add cream and fenugreek leaves (Kasuri Methi) at the very end. Overcooking cream can cause it to separate, and fenugreek leaves lose their aroma if cooked too long.
article:
Butter Chicken, known in India as Murgh Makhani, is a dish that needs little introduction. Revered globally for its incredibly rich, creamy, and subtly sweet yet tangy tomato-based gravy, it’s a cornerstone of Indian cuisine. Perfect as an Indian lunch recipe, this beloved classic offers a comforting and deeply satisfying culinary experience, making it a favorite for family meals, special occasions, or simply a delicious weekday treat. If you’ve ever wondered how to recreate that authentic restaurant-quality taste at home, you’ve come to the right place. Get ready to embark on a flavorful journey that will elevate your lunch game to new heights.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, translates literally to "chicken with butter." Its origins trace back to the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi in the 1950s, where it was created by Kundan Lal Gujral. The story goes that leftover tandoori chicken was simmered in a rich tomato gravy enriched with butter and cream to prevent it from drying out. The result was a culinary masterpiece that quickly gained popularity, becoming one of India's most iconic dishes.

At its heart, Butter Chicken features succulent pieces of chicken (often marinated and lightly grilled or pan-fried) bathed in a luxurious gravy. This gravy is typically made from tomatoes, onions, ginger, garlic, and a blend of aromatic spices like garam masala, cumin, and coriander. What truly sets it apart is the generous addition of butter and cream, which impart an unparalleled silkiness and depth of flavor. A touch of kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) adds a distinctive, slightly bitter, and earthy aroma that is quintessential to authentic Murgh Makhani. It’s a dish that perfectly balances sweet, savory, and tangy notes, creating a harmonious symphony of flavors that is incredibly appealing, especially as a hearty and flavorful Indian lunch.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting the perfect Butter Chicken requires a few key components, each playing a vital role in building its complex flavor profile.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   1.5 lbs boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain full-fat yogurt
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 tsp red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, or regular for heat)
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1 tsp garam masala
*   1 tbsp lemon juice
*   1/2 tsp salt

For the Gravy:
*   2 tbsp ghee or unsalted butter, plus more for finishing
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 (28 oz) can crushed tomatoes or 4-5 large fresh tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup raw cashews (soaked in warm water for 15-20 minutes, then drained)
*   2 green cardamom pods
*   1 inch cinnamon stick
*   2-3 cloves
*   1 bay leaf
*   1 tsp coriander powder
*   1/2 tsp cumin powder
*   1 tsp red chili powder (adjust to taste)
*   1/4 tsp turmeric powder
*   1 tsp garam masala
*   1 tbsp kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), lightly crushed
*   1-2 tbsp sugar (to balance acidity)
*   1/2 cup heavy cream, plus more for garnish
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps to create an unforgettable Butter Chicken for your next Indian lunch.

**Step 1: Marinate the Chicken**
In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor and tenderness.

**Step 2: Cook the Chicken**
Heat 1 tablespoon of ghee or butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until lightly browned and cooked through. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

**Step 3: Prepare the Gravy Base**
In the same pan, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of ghee or butter. Add the whole spices (cardamom, cinnamon stick, cloves, bay leaf) and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the chopped onions and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until the raw smell disappears.

**Step 4: Build the Gravy Flavors**
Add the crushed tomatoes (or fresh pureed tomatoes) and the soaked cashews to the pan. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes begin to thicken. Now, add the ground spices: coriander powder, cumin powder, red chili powder, turmeric powder, and garam masala. Cook for another 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, allowing the spices to toast and their aromas to develop. Add about 1/2 cup of water, bring to a simmer, then cover and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.

**Step 5: Blend the Gravy**
Remove the bay leaf and cinnamon stick. Carefully transfer the gravy mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. For an extra-velvety texture, you can pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the clean pan. This step is crucial for achieving that signature restaurant-style smoothness.

**Step 6: Finish the Gravy**
Return the smooth gravy to the pan over medium-low heat. Add 2 tablespoons of unsalted butter, the kasuri methi (crushed between your palms to release its aroma), and the sugar. Stir until the butter melts and the sugar dissolves. Stir in the heavy cream. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to deepen and the gravy to thicken slightly. Taste and adjust salt if needed.

**Step 7: Combine and Serve**
Add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering gravy. Stir gently to coat the chicken completely. Let it simmer for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors of the gravy. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and a swirl of extra cream or a small pat of butter just before serving.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The yogurt and lemon juice tenderize the chicken and infuse it with flavor, crucial for perfect Butter Chicken.
*   **Blend and Strain:** For that truly authentic, silky-smooth restaurant-style gravy, blending the base thoroughly and then straining it through a fine-mesh sieve is highly recommended. It removes any fibrous bits, creating an incredibly luxurious texture.
*   **Quality Ingredients:** Use good quality canned crushed tomatoes (San Marzano if possible) and fresh, full-fat dairy products. The butter and cream are central to the dish's richness.
*   **Toast Kasuri Methi:** Lightly toasting kasuri methi in a dry pan for a few seconds before crushing and adding it will intensify its unique fragrance, adding depth to your Murgh Makhani.
*   **Balance Flavors:** Butter Chicken is all about balance. The sugar helps cut the acidity of the tomatoes, while the spices provide warmth without overwhelming. Adjust these to your personal preference.
*   **Low and Slow:** After adding the chicken to the gravy, let it simmer gently on low heat. This allows the chicken to fully absorb the flavors and keeps it tender.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a versatile dish that pairs beautifully with a variety of accompaniments, making it a fantastic Indian lunch option.
*   **Naan Bread:** The classic pairing! Warm, fluffy naan bread is perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich gravy. Garlic naan or butter naan elevate the experience even further.
*   **Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or fragrant jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a lovely contrast to the creamy curry and helps soak up the delicious sauce.
*   **Roti or Paratha:** Other Indian flatbreads like soft roti or flaky paratha are also excellent choices.
*   **Side Salad:** A simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, onion with lemon and cilantro) offers a refreshing crunch that balances the richness of the curry.
*   **Raita:** A cooling yogurt dip like cucumber raita can provide a pleasant contrast to the warmth of the spices.
*   **Pickles and Chutneys:** A small dollop of mango pickle or mint chutney can add an extra layer of flavor and zest.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is perfect, there are many ways to adapt it to dietary needs or personal preferences.

*   **Paneer Makhani:** For a delicious vegetarian version, simply substitute the chicken with cubes of paneer (Indian cottage cheese). Pan-fry the paneer lightly before adding it to the gravy. Tofu can also be used for a vegan option.
*   **Dairy-Free:** To make Murgh Makhani dairy-free, use coconut oil or a plant-based butter alternative. For the cream, substitute with full-fat coconut milk or a cashew cream (made by blending soaked cashews with water until smooth) for a similar rich texture.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the red chili powder to your liking. For more heat, add a finely chopped green chili along with the ginger-garlic paste. For a milder version, reduce the chili powder or omit it entirely. Kashmiri chili powder offers vibrant color with less heat.
*   **Healthier Twist:** To reduce calories, use less butter and cream, or opt for a lighter cream alternative. You can also grill the chicken instead of pan-frying it. Adding some finely chopped vegetables (like bell peppers or peas) to the gravy can also boost nutrition.
*   **Quick Version:** While the authentic recipe takes time, you can cut corners by using pre-cooked tandoori chicken or a high-quality store-bought butter chicken paste as a base, significantly reducing preparation time for a speedy Indian lunch.

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is more than just a dish; it's a culinary experience that delights the senses. Its comforting warmth, creamy texture, and complex flavors make it an unparalleled choice for an Indian lunch or any meal. By following these steps and tips, you can confidently recreate this beloved classic in your own kitchen, bringing the taste of India right to your dining table. Enjoy the process, savor the aroma, and delight in every spoonful of your homemade Murgh Makhani!
